title: How do people use AI, from everyday help to seemingly alien intellectual capability?
original_curiosity: I want to investigate the landscape of human–AI intellectual symbiosis, from ordinary users through the 90th, 99th, 99.9th percentiles, and eventually what we might call alien-level intelligence or capability.
parent_purpose: Understand the whole human–AI symbiosis distribution and expand my ability to learn, investigate and engineer with AI, without mystifying exceptional practitioners.
framing: Retain the ordinary / 90th / 99th / 99.9th / frontier-alien strata as provisional sampling targets. These are not empirically ranked populations: measured percentiles require a cohort, outcome, observation procedure, and calibration data. Treat achievements, transferable competence, resources, and different domain specialties separately.

possible_perspectives: Achievement: what was produced and how strongly was it verified
Practice: what the human and AI each did
Transfer: what a nonexpert or another expert could reproduce
Economics: time, cost, attention and reliability
Generativity: which capabilities improve the next investigation
selection_rule: Expand branches only where plausible answers would change what to learn, compare or build; never manufacture an exhaustive tier ladder.
guidance: Use ordinary, curious questions first (RSM-01.03). Branch into possible answers and their consequences (RSM-02.08). Keep candidate evidence separate from established conclusions (RSM-01.04). Distinguish question trees from investigation trees (RSM-05). Explicitly cover ordinary AI use, plausible 90th/99th/99.9th percentile strata, first-person engineering workflows, frontier cases, and their social ecosystems. Demystify exceptional cases through concrete action traces, resources, failures and achievable reconstructions; do not conflate publicity, credentials, prompts and general capability.
original_prompt: I want to investigate the landscape of human–AI intellectual symbiosis, from ordinary users through the 90th, 99th, 99.9th percentiles, and eventually what we might call alien-level intelligence or capability. I'm interested in how the most capable people use AI to accomplish extraordinary intellectual and engineering work. For example, consider Levent Alpöge's reported use of Claude in pursuing a proof of the Riemann hypothesis. Following RSM and FKEN, let's develop a rich question landscape and investigation tree. I want to discover the people, techniques, workflows, projects, tools, communities, and constituent capabilities that distinguish these levels. Importantly, don't just admire extraordinary outcomes or reduce everything to prompting. Investigate how the capabilities compose, what makes them effective, and how we could progressively reproduce, acquire, and surpass them. The investigations should completely demystify what they did and soften the idea of the 'untouchable legend', while studying average users, percentile tiers, and people using AI in ways similar to mine.

sampling_design.calibration_rule: Do not assign actual percentile ranks to people or workflows based on a few anecdotes. Define a reference population, a task family, a measure of independently verified performance or capability and a representative sample first.
sampling_axes: accessibility for novice, skilled individual, specialist or institution
biases_to_watch: model generation confounded with human expertise
apparently simple prompts hiding extensive preparation

demystification_contract.purpose: Replace reverence for an outcome or person with inspectable mechanisms, evidence and reproducible capabilities. Preserve real differences in expertise and resources.
case_questions: What problem did this person actually choose, and why?
What was already known or prepared before AI entered?
Exactly what did the human ask, decide, reject, test, revise and contribute?
What did the model produce and what could it do without the human?
Which tools, references, infrastructure, collaborators and prior expertise were essential?
How many failed approaches, retries and intermediate steps occurred?
What was observed, checked and independently reproduced?
What would the simplest lower-resource reconstruction look like?
Which capability can a capable beginner learn, which requires deliberate practice and which requires deep domain expertise?
What remains unexplained or currently inaccessible, and what evidence would resolve it?
demystification_contract.anti_myth_rule: Do not replace a legend with a simplistic 'anyone can do it' story. Distinguish replicable method, expertise, unusually favorable problem selection, institution-scale resources and unexplained residuals.

presentation_note: The why_ask field is reader-facing subject context, not instructions to the assistant, editor, or investigator. Procedural priorities, source skepticism, evidence certification rules, and editorial direction are recorded in investigation metadata instead.
fieldwork_link_rule: fieldwork_case_ids link candidate questions to case records in fieldwork.json; case observations do not certify the question tree's possible answers.

curiosity_atlas.purpose: Begin from everyday uses, frustrations, professional ambitions or extraordinary claims, then encounter the relevant technical explanations, evidence and contrasting cases without flattening the investigation.

curiosity_atlas.entry_policy: Ordinary questions identify a starting concern, not a ceiling on technical depth. A case may support several entries without copying case evidence.

navigation_bridges.question: Which claim or result is actually supported?

choices.label: An answer or citation sounds plausible
choices.distinguishing_question: Does the cited source support the precise proposition, and can a separate check falsify it?
choices.why: Generating a convincing assertion is distinct from retrieving a source, interpreting it correctly and verifying the intended claim.

choices.label: A claimed theorem or scientific result is formalized
choices.distinguishing_question: Can the artifact be independently replayed, and does its formal statement match the claimed mathematical theorem?
choices.why: A proof checker can validate derivations relative to formal assumptions while leaving specification equivalence as an independent obligation.

navigation_bridges.question: What would establish useful, correct behavior?

choices.label: A generated app compiles or a demo looks good
choices.distinguishing_question: Does a representative task succeed under real input, integration boundaries and failure/restart conditions?
choices.why: Compilation, unit checks, screenshots and sustained practical utility certify different claims. Tests must attack the uncertainty that matters.

choices.label: An evaluator can choose among AI candidates
choices.distinguishing_question: Can the score be gamed or diverge from actual human intent?
choices.why: A cheap, faithful evaluator turns generation into iterative search; a misaligned oracle can efficiently optimize the wrong objective.

navigation_bridges.question: What state makes the work recoverable?

choices.label: A new conversation cannot reconstruct project intent
choices.technical_title: Persisted functional contract versus transient conversation
choices.distinguishing_question: Can a new participant recover the goal, current working state and unresolved decisions from durable artifacts?
choices.why: Message history, source code, evaluated behavior and intentional requirements are not interchangeable stores of project knowledge.

choices.label: A large mistaken edit set must be repaired
choices.technical_title: Known-good baselines, diffs and causal fault localization
choices.distinguishing_question: Which change first violated a representative requirement and can it be reverted independently?
choices.why: Recovery uses inspectable changes and real failure evidence; blind retries add states without explaining the break.

navigation_bridges.question: Did the user acquire transferable capability?

choices.label: AI helped complete today's task
choices.distinguishing_question: Can the person solve a meaningfully different task without identical AI scaffolding?
choices.why: Task completion is not proof of retained competence; discriminate assistance, operational understanding and reusable tacit skill.

choices.label: A famous system used unusual resources
choices.distinguishing_question: What smaller project preserves the essential causal mechanism while removing unrelated scale?
choices.why: Copying an entire system can be less informative than reproducing its evaluator, coordination contract or domain-specific insight.

navigation_bridges.question: Which decisions require human authority or expertise?

choices.label: The agent could continue, but the consequences matter
choices.technical_title: Delegation and escalation as a control policy
choices.distinguishing_question: Are decisions reversible, independently checkable and consistent with the user's functional intent?
choices.why: More autonomy is not automatically more useful; escalation can be the correct behavior at consequential uncertainty.

choices.label: A result depended on expert intervention
choices.technical_title: Human causal contribution versus model generation
choices.distinguishing_question: Which problem choices, analogies, rejections and corrections materially changed the trajectory?
choices.why: The final artifact alone cannot identify who supplied each decisive constraint or whether another person could reproduce it.

navigation_bridges.question: Can agents work independently without destructive interference?

choices.label: Tasks have separable contracts and cheap tests
choices.distinguishing_question: Can results be developed and evaluated independently, then integrated without ambiguous ownership?
choices.why: Parallel work pays off when dependency edges are sparse enough and the verification cost is controlled.

choices.label: Errors share state and need one causal explanation
choices.distinguishing_question: Does changing one part invalidate assumptions and observations elsewhere?
choices.why: Strongly coupled faults require a coherent evolving model; spawning agents can multiply inconsistent local fixes.

navigation_bridges.question: What made the extraordinary result possible?

choices.label: An achievement seems far beyond ordinary users
choices.technical_title: Reconstructable action trace and skill/resource factoring
choices.distinguishing_question: Which hidden dependencies, failed attempts, expert interventions and external tools were necessary?
choices.why: A claim becomes learnable when observable decisions and causal mechanisms replace prestige labels, without pretending expertise disappears.

choices.label: The project improved through iterative generation
choices.distinguishing_question: What observable score or test made a candidate meaningfully better, and how was that score validated?
choices.why: Evaluation can amplify search but only where the objective represents the real goal; uncaptured expertise and invalid benchmarks remain limits.

navigation_bridges.question: Who is being compared, on what task, with what measurement?

choices.label: Many people use AI but few outcomes are measured
choices.technical_title: Usage population versus independently measured performance
choices.distinguishing_question: Does the evidence count conversations, self-reported activity, completed tasks or independently verified outcomes?
choices.why: Aggregate message proportions cannot establish an individual's ability or rank in real engineering performance.

choices.label: Exceptional examples dominate the discussion
choices.distinguishing_question: What would the result be with equal task difficulty, compute, prior expertise and verification?
choices.why: Visible frontier accomplishments are selected samples; apparent percentiles have no meaning without a defined cohort and metric.

navigation_bridges.question: Did the tool reduce real work?

choices.label: Generation was quick but reviewing was expensive
choices.distinguishing_question: How much time elapsed from understanding the task through accepted integration and later correction?
choices.why: Model speed cannot substitute for total task cost; review burden and rework can exceed generation gains.

choices.label: More agents or compute appear to increase capability
choices.technical_title: Marginal output versus coordination and inference budget
choices.distinguishing_question: Does an additional agent improve net correct progress after counting integration, duplicated work and retries?
choices.why: The optimal number of agents depends on task independence, evaluator quality, compute and human attention.
